name: scoop-install
body: Windows users install via a Scoop bucket: `scoop bucket add kalide https://github.com/really-knows-ai/kalide` then `scoop install kalide` (manifest `bucket/kalide.json`); `scoop update kalide` upgrades. The manifest uses Scoop's standard `architecture` block: `64bit` with `url` + `hash` for `kalide-windows-amd64` (always), and `arm64` with `url` + `hash` for `kalide-windows-arm64` only when that target was released (otherwise no arm64 entry). URLs are plain public release-download URLs (`https://github.com/really-knows-ai/kalide/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/kalide-windows-<arch>`, renamed to `kalide.exe` via the `#/kalide.exe` fragment or equivalent), fetched anonymously. No token, `KALIDE_GITHUB_TOKEN`, or `pre_install` download script. `bucket/README.md` documents this tokenless flow. AC: on a clean Windows x64 machine (and on Windows ARM when windows/arm64 is supported) with no GitHub credentials, install succeeds and `kalide` runs; `bucket/kalide.json` has no `pre_install` and no reference to `KALIDE_GITHUB_TOKEN`; `bucket/README.md` mentions no token.
